key_insight: Physics-informed subsampling enabled a tabular foundation model to accurately predict full dielectric spectra of Mo-W-S-Se-Te TMD alloys from limited ab initio data.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable route to screen and design composition-tunable 2D optoelectronic materials without exhaustive first-principles calculations.
method: Generated 99 DFT-calculated alloy structures across binary to quinary Mo-W-S-Se-Te compositions.
Trained a TabPFN regressor on quaternary alloys using energy subsampling concentrated above the band gap.
Compared against Extra Trees and XGBoost, then predicted derived optical properties and tested zero-shot transfer.
evidence_signal: On held-out quaternary alloys, the TabPFN achieved R2 > 0.98 and MAE < 0.10 for all four dielectric components, and it reached R2 > 0.97 on zero-shot quinary predictions.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the physics-informed sampling design and the limited 99-structure dataset, so broader generalization should be validated on additional compositions and materials systems.
paper_title: Machine learning based prediction of optical properties in two-dimensional Mo-W-S-Se-Te transition-metal dichalcogenide alloys through physics-informed sampling
